answer: Staged Reputation Bonding. New wallets start in a hollow tier where every economic action (transfers, listings, votes) requires a small deposit matched against an opaque opal-seeded penalty pool. If a cluster of wallets is flagged by graph analysis, deposits are slashed beyond their balance into that shared pool, so the operator loses capital tied to their real identities. To park sybils, they must harbor enough pre-funded deposits to cover cluster-wide slashing, making each fake identity cost roughly 40x a normal account's annual fees.
